verify.note: Each hook against the original from one state: every register with R and all memory (the bitmap too) at the draw hook, the erase-only entries, the clears, the pace window's entries and ends and every draw from its entry; the object's sprites against a model of the figure, and the model against the original's own plot wherever the entry draws without erasing (the plotter XORs); the colour paint stores nothing and leaves everything else the game's; the IM 1 handler of the alt ROM image against Sinclair's at every interrupt; unit cases over every graphic.

status.title: Cookie
status.build: cookie_sprites.nex faaacc0b (the game draws as it does; every figure a sprite on the same pixels in its own colour; the colour paint stores nothing; loading screen) + enhanced 7df95fe3 (34 pictures painted with 12 fixed colours, a first pass; a pixel left unpainted keeps the game's colour)
status.software: Verify IDENTICAL on two whole machine-played recordings (40,426 frames), both builds: 106,799 figures as sprites, 12,817,707 sprite pixels against the figure's model (itself checked against the original's plot at every draw-only entry) and, on Enhanced, every pixel's colour against the painted map; every register with R and all memory at every hook; the IM 1 handler compared at 32,491 interrupts; unit PASS on both builds (1,632 graphic cases over all 34 graphics, negative control 40 of 40); 6 of 6 broken builds detected; ROM path check pass
status.next: a recording played by hand into later levels; hardware test

techniques.target: the game's plotter and bitmap unchanged; each object's sprites lie on the pixels it plots, in the object's colour; the colour paint's store becomes a read
HLIB_R_IN / hlib_r_set / HLIB_R_OUT in every hook (the game reads R)
HLIB_SPEED_IN at the plot's entries, HLIB_SPEED_OUT at their ends: the set-up runs at 28 MHz and pays for the draw hook
Sinclair's ROM as the alt image with the hooks at 0x386E (0xFF there); the game runs the ROM's IM 1 handler, compared at every interrupt
a painted set changes only the patterns' nibbles and 13 fixed palette colours (nibbles 2-14 of every offset): nibble 1 stays the object's ink at run time; the hooks are the same

pacing.coverage: Two machine-played recordings (40,424 frames); every pace site compared in the replay. No JNext or hardware timing.
pacing.result: The main loop is not frame-synced. The plot's set-up, a fixed stretch a draw, runs at 28 MHz and pays for the draw hook (as Jetpac 1.3); the colour paint takes the original's time to the T state (its store is a read). Not measured as a whole.

dependencies.coverage: Every screen writer of the first recording (survey); every CALL and JP from the handlers into the plot code listed (all use the standard entries); the colour paint's 14 CALLs and JPs checked by the build; all 34 graphics of the type table through the plotter in the unit cases.
dependencies.result: The bitmap and all game memory but the colour cells stay the original's. The game runs the ROM's IM 1 handler: the alt ROM image is Sinclair's. It reads R: every hook leaves R as the original. It rewrites the column limit of its colour paint and the shift of its row routine as it runs: both are left to it (the paint is changed by one byte in place). A 16K game: nothing reads or writes above 0x7FFF, where the hook RAM is.

feasibility.decision: As Jetpac's published patch (owner 2026-11-20: 'Let's finish off the ultimate games'): the game's own colours, moving figures as sprites.
feasibility.next_experiment: A recording played by hand into later levels; hardware: the checklist in games/cookie.md; the game's speed against the original over a minute of play: within 2%.
